{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-wy-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"3c7d6fe53cab5f9d1d17b499268f365f248a9a2b04fa09fc7a00643a9d253b89","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-wy-class-c:lineage:66","source_registry_sha256":"f2806994ac56e29c3588fb4e8e2cc870c5f64d0616933994765d31d7841ccbe9","source_liveness_sha256":"e9e98c5695424e30c400f1e14b2593178d09ca723f8f00581c9655dcae32ca6c"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Driving definitions — C.01","heading":"C — Driving definitions","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Driving definitions
FACT_ID: sec15-F01 | anchor: A01
Authorized emergency vehicles include fire, police and ambulance vehicles and others authorized by statute. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec15-F02 | anchor: A01
The glossary defines a bicycle as a human-powered vehicle with two tandem wheels, excluding scooters and similar devices. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec15-F03 | anchor: A01
The handbook classifies bicycles as vehicles that may use Wyoming public roads. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec15-F04 | anchor: A01
The handbook recommends a correctly fitted, Consumer Product Safety Certified bicycle helmet even though it says a helmet is not legally required. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec15-F05 | anchor: A01
The glossary's blind spots lie near the rear corners on both sides and are not visible in rearview mirrors. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec15-F06 | anchor: A01
Turn the head to view the glossary's blind-spot areas. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec15-F07 | anchor: A01
BAC stands for Blood Alcohol Concentration and refers to alcohol in the bloodstream. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec15-F08 | anchor: A01
Brakes are the devices used to stop a vehicle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec15-F09 | anchor: A01
A critical object is anything that could require slowing, accelerating or turning, including a person, vehicle or animal. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec15-F10 | anchor: A01
A crosswalk is a place where people may legally cross a street or highway. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec15-F11 | anchor: A01
A crosswalk may be marked or unmarked. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec15-F12 | anchor: A01
For an unmarked crosswalk, the glossary uses imaginary lines connecting sidewalks across the roadway. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec15-F13 | anchor: A01
DWUI means operating a vehicle while under the influence of alcohol or a controlled substance. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec15-F14 | anchor: A01
The glossary's emancipated minor is at least 17 and is or was married, serves in the United States military, or has district-court emancipation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec15-F15 | anchor: A01
An emancipated minor may request that status on a Wyoming license by applying to the department and paying the required fee. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec15-F16 | anchor: A01
A traffic gap is enough open space between vehicles for another vehicle to enter safely. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec15-F17 | anchor: A01
A helmet is protective headgear. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0091]

FACT_ID: sec15-F18 | anchor: A02
Hydroplaning means the tires ride on a thin water layer instead of the road. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec15-F19 | anchor: A02
An intersection is the area where streets or highways meet or cross. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec15-F20 | anchor: A02
A lane is a roadway section for one line of vehicles. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec15-F21 | anchor: A02
A median separates roadways and may consist of grass, concrete or other material. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec15-F22 | anchor: A02
Riding on, over or across a median is unlawful under the glossary's rule. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec15-F23 | anchor: A02
Merging traffic occurs when two moving traffic lanes come together, such as at an interstate entrance. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec15-F24 | anchor: A02
A motor vehicle is self-propelled by power other than human muscle and transports people or property on public highways. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec15-F25 | anchor: A02
The glossary includes motorcycles and mopeds as motor vehicles. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec15-F26 | anchor: A02
A moving violation involves control or lack of control while a motor vehicle is moving and results in a conviction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0092]

FACT_ID: sec15-F27 | anchor: A02
A moving-violation conviction can include driving contrary to a corrective-lens or outside-mirror restriction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-wy-c:wyoming-department-of-transportation-dri:handbook:pdf-0092]

Misconceptions: Suspension is temporary removal, while revocation terminates the driving privilege; a crosswalk need not have painted markings.
Mnemonics: Recall index: term, scope, condition; this organizer adds no eligibility route to a definition.
Glossary: Recall groups: road geometry, sight and space, vehicle categories and licensing status.
Dynamic facts: Licensing and residency definitions are edition-bound. Fee amounts, agency street addresses, historic class-renewal policy and unverified immigration terminology are excluded from stable learner facts.
